correctness.rationale: For any six-element set the affine rank is 3, 4, or 5. The four affine classes are exhaustive because the unique rank-four relation is an even circuit of length 4 or 6. Explicit integer Walsh polynomial evaluations give the four complete magnitude histograms and norms, while flat-counting yields all four closed multiplicity formulas; 1–5 point affine types prove the threshold. The packaged checker exhausts all supports of size up to 6 in dimensions 3, 4, 5 and prints CHECK_PASS. Its finite checks confirm but do not substitute for the general affine/classification proof.

value.rationale: The Fourier algebra norm is the central exact invariant in quantitative idempotent-set Fourier analysis. The least indicator-support size producing norm >2 is a natural sharp boundary, nontrivially attained only by *dependent* six-circuits while affine-independent six-sets have norm 15/8. The complete classification and dimension-dependent exact multiplicities constitute a motivated natural finite-pattern theorem rather than an arbitrary invariant slice or a renaming of existing bounds.
